intro: Leaks have a habit of hiding for months before you notice them — and by the time you do, the damage is often well underway. In Lockwood, we see a fair number of properties where a slow, undetected leak has quietly soaked into walls, rotted floorboards, or pushed up water bills without anyone realising why. Whether it's a dripping pipe under the kitchen, a hidden leak behind a bathroom wall, or something more serious beneath a concrete floor, getting it found and fixed quickly is the only way to avoid a much bigger job down the line. The good news is that modern leak detection equipment means we rarely need to tear walls apart just to find the source.
localContext: Lockwood's housing stock is a real mix, and that variety throws up different plumbing challenges depending on where you live. The older stone-built properties and period cottages that make up a good chunk of the area were often built with lead or iron pipework that's now well past its best. These older systems are more prone to pinhole leaks, joint failures, and corrosion — and because the pipes often run through thick stone walls or beneath solid floors, locating a leak without specialist equipment can feel like guesswork. Newer modern estates in Lockwood tend to use copper or plastic pipework, which is generally more reliable, but they're not immune to problems either — poor original installation or movement in the ground can cause joints to fail over time. It's also worth knowing that Lockwood sits in a moderately hard water area. While not as severe as parts of the South East, hard water does encourage limescale build-up inside pipes and around joints, which can gradually narrow flow and put extra stress on older fittings — contributing to leaks over time.
serviceDetail: When you call in a leak detection specialist in Lockwood, the first thing they'll do is have a proper conversation about what you've noticed — higher water bills, damp patches, the sound of running water when everything's switched off, or a drop in water pressure. That context helps narrow things down before any equipment comes out. The most common tool used is acoustic leak detection, which picks up the sound of water escaping from a pressurised pipe — it's surprisingly precise and can locate a leak within a few centimetres, even through concrete or stone. Thermal imaging cameras are also used in many cases, particularly useful in Lockwood's older stone properties where pipes run inside walls and floors. For underground supply pipes, tracer gas equipment may be used — a harmless gas is introduced into the pipe, and a sensor detects where it escapes. Once the leak is pinpointed, the plumber will talk you through the repair options before any work begins. Most repairs in domestic properties involve cutting out a small section of damaged pipe, replacing a faulty joint, or resealing a connection. You'll normally have your water back on the same day. Where access is needed through tiling or flooring, the plumber will aim to keep disruption to a minimum and leave the area as tidy as possible.
pricing: In Lockwood, a typical leak detection visit — including the investigation and a straightforward repair — usually falls somewhere between £100 and £300. If the leak is harder to access, involves older pipework in a stone wall, or requires more extensive repair work, costs can rise to £400–£500. Detection-only callouts, where no repair is carried out on the day, generally start around £80–£150 depending on the equipment needed. The age and construction of your property will affect the price — older Lockwood homes with solid floors or thick walls naturally take longer to work through. Always ask for a clear quote before any work starts so there are no surprises.
whyLocal: Choosing a local plumber who knows Lockwood makes a genuine difference. Someone familiar with the area will already have a good idea of what pipework to expect in a 1930s stone terrace versus a modern semi — that local knowledge speeds things up and reduces unnecessary exploratory work. They'll also know which parts of Lockwood have seen ground movement issues or where older infrastructure is more likely to be causing problems. A local tradesperson is also accountable — they're not disappearing after one job, they're working in the community and their reputation matters to them.

faqs.q: How do I know if I have a hidden leak in my Lockwood home?
faqs.a: The most common signs are unexplained rises in your water bill, damp patches on walls or ceilings, the sound of running water when nothing is turned on, or low water pressure with no obvious cause. In older Lockwood properties, musty smells and peeling plaster can also point to a slow leak that's been going on for some time.

faqs.q: Will the plumber need to dig up my floor or break into my walls to find the leak?
faqs.a: Not usually. Modern acoustic and thermal detection equipment means most leaks can be located precisely without any destructive investigation. In Lockwood's older stone-built homes, this is particularly valuable — the aim is always to identify the exact spot before opening anything up, keeping repair work as small and tidy as possible.

faqs.q: Can hard water cause leaks in Lockwood properties?
faqs.a: It's a contributing factor, yes. Lockwood's moderately hard water causes gradual limescale build-up inside pipes and around joints. Over time, this adds pressure to older fittings and can accelerate corrosion in metal pipework. It won't cause a sudden dramatic leak on its own, but it does mean older plumbing systems in the area need a bit more attention.

faqs.q: How long does a typical leak detection and repair job take in Lockwood?
faqs.a: Most jobs are completed within half a day. Detection alone usually takes one to two hours depending on how accessible the pipework is. A straightforward repair — cutting out a damaged section and replacing it — adds another hour or so. More complex cases involving deep-set pipes in older Lockwood stonework may take longer, but your plumber should be upfront about this from the start.
